nodes.name: totient_unit_prefix_exists

nodes.name: totient_unit_prefix_all_bits

nodes.name: totient_unit_prefix_equal_entry
nodes.summary: All unit masks encode the same bits on their common interval.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_succ_intro

nodes.name: totient_unit_choice_mod_one

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_mod_one
nodes.summary: The independently constructed unit count modulo one equals the actual interval length.

nodes.name: totient_functional

nodes.name: totient_bounded

nodes.name: totient_zero_excluded
nodes.summary: Phi keeps the blueprint's positive-domain boundary; auxiliary empty counting does not manufacture Phi(0,0).

nodes.name: totient_one

nodes.name: totient_one_value
nodes.summary: Construct the actual Phi(1,1) count witnesses, including the zero residue.

nodes.name: totient_exists_unique
nodes.summary: Total uniquely determined totient on all positive naturals, independently of the still separate Euler product theorem.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_length_transport
nodes.summary: Transport the actual characteristic and summation traces along equality of interval lengths.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_value_transport
nodes.summary: Changing a proved equal terminal value preserves the real finite count.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_zero_value
nodes.summary: Construct the empty-interval zero count for every modulus, without admitting Phi at modulus zero.

nodes.name: totient_unit_choices_equal_of_equivalence
nodes.summary: Equivalent actual unit predicates have equal independently decided indicator bits.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_interval_balance
nodes.summary: HA induction proves equality of actual count increments on any two pointwise equivalent finite intervals.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_periodic
nodes.summary: The actual common-divisor unit predicate is periodic modulo n, including the degenerate auxiliary modulus zero.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_period_block
nodes.summary: Each complete period contributes exactly the actual count of one canonical residue interval.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_periods
nodes.summary: The actual unit count on k complete periods equals k times the actual canonical count.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_pointwise_equal
nodes.summary: Equal actual unit predicates throughout a finite prefix have equal witnessed cardinalities.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_modulus_transport
nodes.summary: A proved equal modulus preserves the actual finite count without changing its interval.

nodes.name: totient_value_transport
nodes.summary: A proved equal value preserves the positive-domain actual totient graph.

nodes.name: totient_modulus_transport
nodes.summary: A proved equal positive modulus preserves both the unit predicate and its canonical residue interval.

nodes.name: totient_divisor_reflexive
nodes.summary: Every natural divides itself with the explicit quotient one.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_divisor_right
nodes.summary: Every divisor of a modulus is coprime to each unit of that modulus.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_product_iff
nodes.summary: Units of a product are exactly the simultaneous units of both factors, without a coprime-moduli assumption.

nodes.name: totient_prime_coprime_iff_nondivisor
nodes.summary: For a prime modulus the independently defined unit predicate is equivalent to nondivisibility.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_repeated_factor
nodes.summary: Adjoining a factor already dividing the modulus leaves the unit predicate unchanged.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_cancel_unit_factor
nodes.summary: Multiplication by a unit preserves common-divisor coprimality at every index.

nodes.name: totient_prime_multiple_is_not_unit
nodes.summary: A multiple of p is never a unit modulo n*p, including j=0.

nodes.name: totient_nonzero_prime_block_offset_not_divisible
nodes.summary: The positive offsets inside a prime-width block cannot be multiples of its width.

nodes.name: totient_prime_block_positive_offset_units
nodes.summary: Apart from its first index, each p-wide block has exactly the same unit mask for n and n*p.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_repeated_prime_factor
nodes.summary: When p already divides n, the actual canonical unit count of n*p is p times that of n.

nodes.name: totient_unit_choice_transport
nodes.summary: Transport an actually decided characteristic bit along proved equivalence of its predicates.

nodes.name: totient_prime_block_end
nodes.summary: The one first index and h remaining indices are exactly a block of width p=S h.

nodes.name: totient_count_defect_step
nodes.summary: Subtraction-free cancellation propagates an exact finite count defect by one actual bit.

nodes.name: totient_new_prime_block_count_balance
nodes.summary: A genuine p-wide block loses exactly the unit indicator of j at its first index p*j; all positive offsets are unchanged.

nodes.name: totient_new_prime_multiple_blocks_balance
nodes.summary: Induction on the number of prime-width blocks counts all removed multiples using the actual unit count of their quotients.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_new_prime_balance
nodes.summary: For a new prime factor, the removed multiples account for exactly one old canonical unit count among p periods.

nodes.name: totient_unit_count_new_prime_factor
nodes.summary: The actual canonical unit count of n*p is (p-1) times that of n when p is prime and coprime to n.

nodes.name: totient_repeated_prime_factor
nodes.summary: Construct Phi(n*p,p*Phi(n)) when the prime p already divides n, using the actual finite unit-count identity.

nodes.name: totient_new_prime_factor
nodes.summary: Construct Phi(n*p,(p-1)*Phi(n)) for a new prime factor; the predecessor is represented by p=S h.

nodes.name: totient_prime_value
nodes.summary: A prime has exactly p-1 canonical units, with all beta witnesses constructed from Phi(1,1).

nodes.name: totient_prime_power_successor_value
nodes.summary: Induction proves Phi(p^(e+1))=(p-1)*p^e for the independent unit count, starting with the prime case.

nodes.name: totient_prime_power_value
nodes.summary: For every positive prime exponent, construct p-1, e-1, the actual preceding power, and its product giving the uniquely defined totient.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_divisor_left
nodes.summary: Coprimality passes to any genuinely witnessed divisor on the left.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_multiplication_prime_step
nodes.summary: One genuine prime-factor step preserves multiplicativity, separating the new-prime and repeated-prime cases constructively.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_multiplicative_from_prime_list
nodes.summary: Induction on an actual beta-coded prime list proves multiplicativity; no sorting, supplied count, or omitted prime-factor case is assumed.

nodes.name: totient_coprime_multiplicative
nodes.summary: The actual totient is multiplicative for every pair of positive coprime moduli; the needed finite prime list is constructed, not supplied.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_exists
nodes.summary: Construct the arithmetic Euler factor from the actual prime and positive exponent, independently of any unit count.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_correct
nodes.summary: The independently computed Euler factor equals the actual unit count of its prime power.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_functional
nodes.summary: Predecessor and beta-encoding choices cannot change the computed arithmetic Euler factor.

nodes.name: totient_prime_entries_decoded_power
nodes.summary: Every actually decoded support power has its prime, positive exponent and genuine power witnesses at the same index.

nodes.name: totient_prime_entries_selected_power
nodes.summary: The selected prime/exponent beta entries refer to the same actual power, not merely some unrelated factorization witnesses.

nodes.name: totient_prime_support_powers_pairwise_coprime
nodes.summary: Distinct prime entries force their actual prime-power factors to be pairwise coprime; injectivity supplies the needed inequality witnesses.

nodes.name: totient_pairwise_coprime_product_fold
nodes.summary: Actual beta products of pairwise coprime moduli multiply their actual totient counts, including the empty product one.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_prefix_empty
nodes.summary: The empty actual Euler-factor list has no entries or artificial zero-exponent factors.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_prefix_drop_last
nodes.summary: A prefix retains all actual prime, exponent, factor, and preceding-power witnesses.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_prefix_append
nodes.summary: Actually append the computed Euler factor while preserving every earlier beta-decoded value and its arithmetic witnesses.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_prefix_exists
nodes.summary: HA induction constructs the full beta-coded list of p^(e-1)*(p-1) from actual positive prime-valuation entries.

nodes.name: totient_euler_factor_prefix_counts
nodes.summary: The factor and support lists share the very same decoded prime and exponent at each index, so each Euler factor is the actual totient of its power.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_from_support
nodes.summary: The actual Euler-factor product over complete distinct prime-valuation support equals the independently defined unit count of n.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_correct
nodes.summary: Every genuine complete Euler product computes Phi; this is proved, not stipulated in either definition.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_exists
nodes.summary: For every positive n construct complete distinct valuation support, every preceding power and Euler factor, and their actual finite product.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_functional
nodes.summary: Changing the complete support ordering or any beta code cannot change the Euler-product value.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_from_count
nodes.summary: Every actual totient count has a fully constructed complete prime-support Euler product with that exact value.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_iff
nodes.summary: The independently defined actual unit count and complete prime-support Euler product are equivalent on precisely the positive domain.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_one
nodes.summary: At n=1 construct the genuinely empty prime support and empty Euler-factor product one, with every list code explicitly zero.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_zero_excluded
nodes.summary: The Euler product preserves the positive domain: no finite complete-support product is fabricated for zero.

nodes.name: totient_euler_product_formula
nodes.summary: G006: for every positive n construct an actual prime factorization, the actual unit count, and its equal product of p^(Val(p,n)-1)*(p-1) over every distinct prime divisor; n=1 gives the empty product one.

nodes.name: Lt
nodes.summary: Witness-defined strict order on natural numbers.

nodes.name: BetaAt
nodes.summary: x is the bounded beta-decoded value at index i.

nodes.name: Dvd
nodes.summary: The natural number d divides n.

nodes.name: Coprime
nodes.summary: Every common divisor of a and b is one.

nodes.name: UnitBitPrefix
nodes.summary: The decoded bit at i<l is one exactly for Coprime(i,n), and zero otherwise. The interval starts at zero.

nodes.name: Sum
nodes.summary: z is the sum of a beta-coded prefix of length l.

nodes.name: UnitCount
nodes.summary: An actual beta sum counts the coprime residues in 0≤i<l. This auxiliary count is total even at modulus zero.

nodes.name: Phi
nodes.summary: Positive n and the actual count of canonical residues i<n coprime to n. Phi(1,1) counts residue zero; Phi excludes n=0.

nodes.name: Prime
nodes.summary: p is nonunit and every factorization of p has a unit factor.

nodes.name: Product
nodes.summary: z is the product of a beta-coded prefix of length l.

nodes.name: Repeat
nodes.summary: The decoded prefix repeats a for l positions.

nodes.name: Pow
nodes.summary: z is the relational e-th power of a.

nodes.name: EulerPrimePowerFactor
nodes.summary: For an actual prime and positive exponent, explicit predecessor and power witnesses compute c=p^(e−1)(p−1). No totient count is assumed.

nodes.name: EulerFactorPrefix
nodes.summary: At every bounded index, the same prime/exponent entries determine the actual Euler factor in the third beta prefix.

nodes.name: InjectivePrefix
nodes.summary: Equal decoded values below l have equal indices.

nodes.name: Le
nodes.summary: Witness-defined non-strict order on natural numbers.

nodes.name: PowerDivides
nodes.summary: The relational power p to exponent e divides n.

nodes.name: BoundedPowerValuation
nodes.summary: e is the greatest exponent at most b for which p to that exponent divides n.

nodes.name: PowerValuation
nodes.summary: e is the canonical bounded p-adic power valuation of n.

nodes.name: PrimeExponentEntries
nodes.summary: Each bounded index simultaneously decodes an actual prime, its positive valuation in n, and the value of that prime power.

nodes.name: PrimeDivisorSupport
nodes.summary: Every actual prime divisor of n occurs at a witnessed index in this prime prefix; no prime divisor may be omitted.

nodes.name: PrimeValuationSupport
nodes.summary: Positive n, distinct actual prime/exponent/power entries, complete coverage of prime divisors, and an actual finite product equal to n. One has the empty support.

nodes.name: EulerProduct
nodes.summary: A complete distinct prime-valuation support, its independently computed Euler factors, and their actual product t. Equality with Phi is a theorem, not a definition.

nodes.name: AllPrime
nodes.summary: Every decoded factor below l is prime.

nodes.name: PrimeFactorList
nodes.summary: A positive number n, an actual length-l beta product equal to n, and prime entries. No sortedness or supplied canonicalization is required.
